references.notes: Assyrian, apart from possible strays. August 1879 Six cases. Receipt inventory: 1879 P 4228. This included, besides other objects, at least 600 tablets or fragments and the Cyrus cylinder, 80-6-17, 1941 (BM 90920), from Amran (WAA Corr: Rassam, 20 November 1879), found before Rassam’s leaving Baghdad, and other tablets from Babylon and Borsippa (Nabu Temple). There was some confusion, at the time of receipt, because the contents of the consignment did not correspond satisfactorily to Daud Thoma’s inventories (see 1897 P 3984, P 4228), which may partially refer to the next consignment. Some uninscribed objects from the August 1879 consignment were eventually registered, like the Cyrus cylinder, with 80-6-17 numbers, and some of the tablets, which had been badly damaged in transit, may be there too; the receipt inventory totals are 999 from Babylon and 109 from Borsippa.
